/-!
# Conjecture 8.12

by D. L. Johnson, E. F. Robertson

Let $D0$ denote the class of finite groups of deficiency zero, i.e. having a
presentation $\langle X \mid R \rangle$ with $|X| = |R|$.

a) Does $D0$ contain any 3-generator $p$-group for $p \geq 5$?

c) Do soluble $D0$-groups have bounded derived length?

d) Which non-abelian simple groups can occur as composition factors of $D0$-groups?

Part d) asks for a description rather than a yes/no answer and is not stated here.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.docstring:
A group $G$ has *deficiency zero* if it has a finite presentation
$\langle X \mid R \rangle$ with $|X| = |R|$: there are a finite set $X$ of generators and a
finite set $R$ of relators in the free group on $X$ with $|R| = |X|$ such that $G$ is
isomorphic to the presented group $\langle X \mid R \rangle$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: PresentedGroup (Mathlib.GroupTheory.PresentedGroup) — used as the building block; Group.FG / Group.rank (only capture generators, not relators); rg for 'deficiency' in Mathlib and the repo found only unrelated number-theoretic/combinatorial uses.
justification.name: Kourovka.«8.12».HasDeficiencyZero
justification.why_needed: Neither Mathlib nor FormalConjecturesForMathlib has a notion of the deficiency of a group or of a deficiency-zero presentation. Defined as: ∃ (X : Type) (_ : Fintype X) (R : Finset (FreeGroup X)), Fintype.card X = R.card ∧ Nonempty (PresentedGroup (R : Set (FreeGroup X)) ≃* G). Finiteness of X and R is required because 'deficiency' is only defined for finite presentations, and without it every finite group would trivially qualify (take an infinite X and R = all relators). Accompanied by a proven @[category test] lemma that the trivial group PUnit has deficiency zero via the empty presentation.

blocks.name: HasDeficiencyZero
blocks.text:
/--
A group $G$ has *deficiency zero* if it has a finite presentation
$\langle X \mid R \rangle$ with $|X| = |R|$: there are a finite set $X$ of generators and a
finite set $R$ of relators in the free group on $X$ with $|R| = |X|$ such that $G$ is
isomorphic to the presented group $\langle X \mid R \rangle$.
-/
def HasDeficiencyZero (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (X : Type) (_ : Fintype X) (R : Finset (FreeGroup X)),
    Fintype.card X = R.card ∧ Nonempty (PresentedGroup (R : Set (FreeGroup X)) ≃* G)

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem hasDeficiencyZero_unit : HasDeficiencyZero Unit :=
  let R : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin 0)) := ∅
  haveI := (PresentedGroup.mk_surjective (R : Set (FreeGroup (Fin 0)))).subsingleton
  haveI := Unique.mk' (PresentedGroup (R : Set (FreeGroup (Fin 0))))
  ⟨Fin 0, inferInstance, R, by simp [R], ⟨MulEquiv.ofUnique⟩⟩

Does $D0$ contain any 3-generator $p$-group for $p \geq 5$?

That is, is there a prime $p \geq 5$ and a finite $p$-group $G$ of deficiency zero whose
minimal number of generators $d(G)$ is exactly $3$? The presentation witnessing deficiency
zero need not itself have $3$ generators.

claims.decomposer_note: Yes/no existential question: does there exist a prime p ≥ 5 and a finite p-group G whose minimal number of generators is exactly 3 (d(G)=3, not merely 'generated by 3 elements') and which admits a finite presentation ⟨X | R⟩ with |X| = |R| (deficiency zero); the group must be finite (D0 is a class of finite groups by definition), and the presentation witnessing deficiency zero need not itself have 3 generators.
claims.reviewer_why: answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (p : ℕ) (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (_ : Finite G), p.Prime ∧ 5 ≤ p ∧ IsPGroup p G ∧ Group.rank G = 3 ∧ HasDeficiencyZero G. Group.rank is Mathlib's minimal number of generators (Nat.find over finite generating sets), so '3-generator' is d(G)=3 exactly as the notes require; p.Prime is added since IsPGroup does not require primality; finiteness is explicit (D0 is a class of finite groups); the deficiency-zero presentation is quantified independently of the 3 generators. All 8 candidates state essentially this; c01 chosen for the literal |X| = |R| definition over a general finite generator type and for theorem names matching the slot IDs and the repo's `<name>.parts.<i>` convention.

claims.decomposer_note: Yes/no question with an implicit quantifier order: does there exist a uniform bound n such that every finite soluble (solvable) group admitting a presentation with |X| = |R| has derived length ≤ n; the bound must be chosen before the group (∃ n, ∀ G …), and 'soluble' means Mathlib's IsSolvable.
claims.reviewer_why: answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G], IsSolvable G → HasDeficiencyZero G → derivedSeries G n = ⊥. The bound n is chosen before the group (∃ n, ∀ G); 'soluble' is Mathlib's IsSolvable; 'derived length ≤ n' is exactly derivedSeries G n = ⊥ since the derived series is antitone. All candidates agree on this statement; c01's version selected for consistency with slot a and its shared definition.

claims.decomposer_note: Open-ended 'which' question whose deliverable is a description of the class of finite non-abelian simple groups isomorphic to a composition factor of some finite deficiency-zero group; neither the statement nor the background asserts a candidate answer (e.g. 'all of them'), so there is no definite Prop to state (only a tautological `{S | …} = answer(sorry)` would be possible).

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.12

by D. L. Johnson, E. F. Robertson

Let $D0$ denote the class of finite groups of deficiency zero, i.e. having a
presentation $\langle X \mid R \rangle$ with $|X| = |R|$.

a) Does $D0$ contain any 3-generator $p$-group for $p \geq 5$?

c) Do soluble $D0$-groups have bounded derived length?

d) Which non-abelian simple groups can occur as composition factors of $D0$-groups?

Part d) asks for a description rather than a yes/no answer and is not stated here.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.12»

/--
A group $G$ has *deficiency zero* if it has a finite presentation
$\langle X \mid R \rangle$ with $|X| = |R|$: there are a finite set $X$ of generators and a
finite set $R$ of relators in the free group on $X$ with $|R| = |X|$ such that $G$ is
isomorphic to the presented group $\langle X \mid R \rangle$.
-/
def HasDeficiencyZero (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (X : Type) (_ : Fintype X) (R : Finset (FreeGroup X)),
    Fintype.card X = R.card ∧ Nonempty (PresentedGroup (R : Set (FreeGroup X)) ≃* G)

/-- The trivial group has deficiency zero: it has the empty presentation
$\langle \varnothing \mid \varnothing \rangle$. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem hasDeficiencyZero_unit : HasDeficiencyZero Unit :=
  let R : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin 0)) := ∅
  haveI := (PresentedGroup.mk_surjective (R : Set (FreeGroup (Fin 0)))).subsingleton
  haveI := Unique.mk' (PresentedGroup (R : Set (FreeGroup (Fin 0))))
  ⟨Fin 0, inferInstance, R, by simp [R], ⟨MulEquiv.ofUnique⟩⟩

/--
Does $D0$ contain any 3-generator $p$-group for $p \geq 5$?

That is, is there a prime $p \geq 5$ and a finite $p$-group $G$ of deficiency zero whose
minimal number of generators $d(G)$ is exactly $3$? The presentation witnessing deficiency
zero need not itself have $3$ generators.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.12».parts.a : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (p : ℕ) (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (_ : Finite G),
      p.Prime ∧ 5 ≤ p ∧ IsPGroup p G ∧ Group.rank G = 3 ∧ HasDeficiencyZero G := by
  sorry

/--
Do soluble $D0$-groups have bounded derived length?

That is, is there an $n$ such that every finite soluble group of deficiency zero has
derived length at most $n$, i.e. the $n$-th term of its derived series is trivial?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.12».parts.c : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G],
      IsSolvable G → HasDeficiencyZero G → derivedSeries G n = ⊥ := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.12»

items: '3-generator p-group' is read as Group.rank G = 3 (minimal number of generators exactly 3), per the decomposition notes; the weaker reading 'generated by 3 elements' would make part a) trivially true (2-generator p-groups of deficiency zero exist for every p).

Relators R are modelled as a Finset (distinct relators) rather than a multiset/list; for finite groups this is equivalent since deficiency > 0 is impossible for a finite group, so a multiset presentation with |X| = |R| already yields a set presentation with |X| = |R|.
Finiteness of G is stated explicitly (Finite G) in both slots rather than folded into HasDeficiencyZero, which is defined for arbitrary groups so it is reusable; D0 = finite ∧ HasDeficiencyZero.
Groups are quantified over Type (universe 0), following the other Kourovka files; every finite group is isomorphic to one in Type, so no generality is lost.
Derived length ≤ n is expressed as derivedSeries G n = ⊥ instead of introducing a derived-length function; this is exactly equivalent since the derived series is antitone.
Group.rank G uses the instance Group.fg_of_finite from [Finite G]; Group.FG is a Prop so the instance choice does not affect the value.

reviewer_notes: All eight candidates are mathematically equivalent (same reading of every term); differences are only naming/style, so no candidate omitted a slot and no omission reasons needed weighing. Part d) ('Which non-abelian simple groups can occur as composition factors') was dropped by the decomposition table as having no statable Prop; all candidates concurred and the final file mentions it only in the module docstring as not stated. Modeling choices a reviewer should know: (1) 'deficiency zero' is encoded with a finite generator type X and a Finset R of relators with Fintype.card X = R.card; counting relators as a set rather than a multiset is equivalent for the finite groups in D0, because a finite group has no presentation with fewer relators than generators (otherwise its abelianization would be infinite). (2) '3-generator' is read as Group.rank G = 3 (minimal number of generators exactly 3); the weaker reading 'generated by 3 elements' would make part a) trivially true (e.g. cyclic p-groups ⟨x | x^p⟩ are in D0), so the strict reading is the intended one and matches the decomposition notes. (3) Groups are quantified over Type (universe 0), following the existing Kourovka files; every finite group has an isomorphic copy there. (4) The final file also includes a `category test` theorem that the trivial group has deficiency zero (test for the bespoke definition, as CONTRIBUTING.md requests). The file compiles standalone and as a repo module with `lake --wfail build` with no warnings other than `declaration uses 'sorry'`.
